reference.title: Scenario 5 — Equation in a procedure step
reference.shortdesc: Consider a numbered procedure where one of the steps contains an equation object — either

section.p: Consider a numbered procedure where one of the steps contains an equation object — either inline within the step command or as a block equation placed immediately after the step text to show a calculation the user must perform.

row.entry: [List Number]: Calculate the load using: [Equation object: P = IV] (block, aligned with step) [List Number]: Record the result.

entry.codeblock: <task id="calculate-load"> <taskbody> <steps> <step> <cmd>Calculate the load using:</cmd> <info> <equation-block> <mathml> <m:math xmlns:m="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <m:mrow> <m:mi>P</m:mi> <m:mo>=</m:mo> <m:mi>I</m:mi> <m:mi>V</m:mi> </m:mrow> </m:math> </mathml> </equation-block> </info> </step> <step> <cmd>Record the result.</cmd> </step> </steps> </taskbody> </task>

section.p: Result: When a block equation is placed immediately after a numbered step and aligned at list level, the converter places it inside the <step><info> element as an <equation-block>, binding it to the parent step. The equation adopts the procedural step's context and is rendered as part of that step's supplementary content, not as a standalone topic-level element.
